source.title: Prediction-error signals in anterior cingulate cortex drive task-switching

confidence_rationale: The strongest CAUSAL grounding for MECH-456's trigger: optogenetic silencing/un-silencing plus two-photon imaging show ACC prediction-error signals are specifically REQUIRED for single-trial switching between two response rules, and the PE signal is LARGER preceding successful transitions -- a graded, causal, single-trial mechanism. This maps onto both DVs in spirit: PE-driven overtake (trigger) and a graded consequence (larger PE -> more successful switch, cf. DV2's graded re-acquisition). Held below 0.8 because task-rule switching in mice is a cognitive-state switch, not an entity/self<->world-config rebinding, and the ACC-circuit specificity does not map onto REE's binder locus.
failure_signatures: Task-switching between two response rules is a cognitive-STATE switch, not a rebinding of an entity/self<->world-configuration; the abstract 'switch when PE says the current model is wrong' transfers, but the bound thing differs.
The causal circuit is ACC + a specific disinhibitory interneuron motif in mouse cortex; REE has no homologous locus, so the mechanism grounds the PRINCIPLE, not REE's implementation.
Larger PE preceding successful transitions is a graded correlate but the single-trial causal test (opto) is on the switch itself, not on a downstream re-acquisition-latency metric like MECH-456 DV2.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In mice trained to respond to identical stimuli under two distinct rules, a prediction-error is used to switch rule in a single trial. Optogenetic silencing and un-silencing plus widefield/two-photon calcium imaging show the anterior cingulate cortex is specifically required for this rapid switching -- but only when it exhibits neural prediction-error signals; those signals are projection-target dependent and are larger preceding successful behavioural transitions, and a disinhibitory interneuron circuit is required to compute them.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the causal, single-trial version of MECH-456's rebinding trigger. Where Weilnhammer shows PE accrual CORRELATES with endogenous switching, Cole et al. show PE is CAUSALLY NECESSARY for a single-trial switch of the operative model, and that the switch is GRADED in the PE magnitude (larger PE -> more successful transition). MECH-456 asserts rebinding is prediction-error / competitor-overtake driven and demands a graded, non-saturating behavioural consequence (DV2). Cole et al. supply the animal-causal analogue of both: a PE that must be present for the switch to happen, scaled to how decisively the current model has failed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The switched thing is a RESPONSE RULE (cognitive set), not a self<->world-configuration binding -- the abstract 'drop the current model when PE says it is wrong' transfers, but the locus and the bound object differ. The causal mechanism is ACC-specific mouse cortical circuitry with no REE homologue, so this grounds the PRINCIPLE (PE causally drives single-trial model switching, graded by error) not REE's binder implementation. Ground-truth tracking (DV1) is present here (there IS a correct rule) but is not separated from the PE-drives-switch result.
mapping.source_context: Head-fixed mice, two-rule stimulus-response task with single-trial rule switches; optogenetic causal manipulation + two-photon and widefield calcium imaging of ACC.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (Nat Commun, causal optogenetics + all-optical + imaging -- rare causal PE result). Mapping fidelity moderate (0.62): PE causally-drives-single-trial-switch and the graded-with-PE finding map onto the trigger and DV2 in spirit, but the switched object is a task rule not an entity binding. Transfer risk moderate-high (0.42): mouse ACC circuit -> latent binder is a principle-level transfer.
